newsitem.title: FINLAND: M-Serla sees better pulp prices later '97.
newsitem.headline: M-Serla sees better pulp prices later '97.

text.p: Finnish pulp producer Metsa-Botnia, 52-percent owned by forest industry group Metsa-Serla Oy, said on Monday pulp prices would improve later in 1997 after remaining weak this winter.
"The winter season will be quite weak," Metsa-Botnia CEO Erkki Varis told a news conference, referring to still high pulp inventories.
"All the signs point towards better prices later in the year," Varis said.

Metsa-Serla director Thomas Nysten said: "Prices of coated papers have turned into a rise. In other paper grades the downward trend continues." Varis and Nysten spoke in connection with the release of Metsa-Serla's 1996 results.
The group's profit after financial items fell to 315 million markka from 1.91 billion in 1995.
Metsa-Serla said it expected a recovery to start in 1997 but the positive impact on earnings was only likely to show in 1998.
"A turn for the better will probably happen this year," Metsa-Serla said in a statement with its 1996 results. "But the results will only be reaped in the next financial year."
